title: Aria object and enemy sprites, boxes and stats
limitations: The native C11 rebuild task exports 348 traced door, enemy and shared-effect sequences, 1,344 indexed frames, 825 unique BMPs, frame boxes, anchors, probes, volleys and all 113 enemy stat records; all 828 files are byte-identical to the former Python writer and guarded by recorded digests. Coverage remains partial because only objects and enemies whose create routine is traced are catalogued: wooden door, the 50 named enemy/palette variants and child frames, the common death flame, blood, smoke, fire, spark, dust, impact, ember and casing effects. The Python object writer is removed.

title: Aria constructor-table enemy batch (Skeleton through Winged Skeleton)
limitations: Ten native enemy identities now load their traced sheets, palettes, frame boxes and constructor states; only first observable patrol, swim, hover and homing loops are connected. Multipart children, attacks, probes, fades, sounds and rewards remain open.

title: Aria Peeping Eye and White Dragon linked children
limitations: Peeping Eye emits its two overlays and six linked static frames; White Dragon emits all nine animation-1 body parts in linked batches. Native polar/affine choreography, attack callbacks, fades, sounds and rewards remain open.

title: Aria early-enemy motion controller wiring
limitations: Dedicated parent motion controllers now dispatch Peeping Eye, White Dragon, Buer, Rock Armor, Giant Ghost and Winged Skeleton movement. Native polar/affine choreography, probes, attacks, fades, sounds and rewards remain open.

title: Aria Peeping Eye polar and White Dragon articulated motion
limitations: Peeping Eye segments target Soma with fixed-point polar offsets; White Dragon parts follow a curved linked chain and forward per-part angles to the renderer. Full attack timing, probes, affine scale/matrix details, damage callbacks, fades, sounds and rewards remain open.

title: Aria White Dragon central affine slot
limitations: The middle linked body record uses the native shared unit-scale affine slot and tracked angle; full scale/matrix choreography, attack timing, damage callbacks, fades, sounds and rewards remain open.

title: Aria Peeping Eye attack entry and polar envelope
limitations: The native 180 by 200 activation window starts a visual wind-up, extension and retraction of the linked polar tendrils. The ROM variant table, exact timing, probes, damage callbacks, fades, sounds and rewards remain open.

title: Aria Peeping Eye timed entry sequence
limitations: The Peeping Eye now runs its traced ten-stage, 40-frame polar extension sequence after its native activation gate. Random target selection, the state-3 variant branch table, probes, damage callbacks, fades, sounds and rewards remain open.

title: Aria Peeping Eye random target steering
limitations: The Peeping Eye now picks its traced 64..112-pixel sideways, 32..80-pixel upward target and steers with native damping, tolerance, speed cap and timeout. The state-3 visual variant table, probes, damage callbacks, fades, sounds and rewards remain open.

title: Aria Bone Pillar and Buer linked components
limitations: Bone Pillar now assembles its native 22-pixel linked tower and Buer emits its linked second direct frame. Per-segment and fire collision, bounce timing, attacks, fades, sounds and rewards remain open.

title: Aria file selection and runtime launch bridge
limitations: The SDL host offers three checksummed portable save files and launches New Game or Continue into the actual room runtime. It is not the native GameModeMainMenuUpdate or SRAM layout; inventory, equipment, souls, flags, play time and save-room writes remain open.

title: Aria native save-room detection and portable checkpoint writes
limitations: The native room exporter carries the global-map save/warp bits in schema v4, while runtime v3 exports remain compatible and detect object 0x1C. Up inside the native Object1C rectangle restores HP and writes room, spawn, HP, moves and play time to the selected portable slot. Native healing animation, Yes/No prompt, object art, sounds, inventory, souls, event/map state and SRAM parity remain open.

title: Aria runtime rooms (background, video memory, BG1 collision, transitions, entities)
limitations: The native importer was source-compared on 342 BG1 collision maps, complete VRAM/palette snapshots for all 343 rooms, 901 expanded static tilemaps and 150929408 rendered RGBA pixels, 342 static-origin RGB composites totaling 61210624 pixels and their byte-identical 183650340-byte BMP representation, plus 342 byte-identical AOSROOM-NATIVE v4 payloads totaling 2035730 bytes with 956416 cells, 725 transitions and 2335 entities. Its atomic writer produces the same 685 private files as the former Python exporter, including the SHA-256 index, and now runs the aria_rooms rebuild task alone; recorded SHA-256 digests guard every native command, both catalog files and every export file. One room has no BG1 payload. The Python renderer remains for editor previews and sprite tooling, not production room export.

title: Soma animation library
limitations: The native C11 rebuild task exports all 83 Soma animations and the one supported knife animation as 382 indexed frames and 152 unique BMPs; all 155 files are byte-identical to the former Python writer and guarded by recorded digests. Animation-specific palette banks are preserved. Knife animation 1 still has unsupported multi-component OAM. The Python writer and its unconsumed preview decoder are removed.

title: Soma weapon records and blade sprites
limitations: The native C11 rebuild task exports all 59 weapon records plus the unarmed record, 60 sprite sequences, 416 indexed frames, 255 unique BMPs and both metadata tables; all 258 files are byte-identical to the former Python writer and guarded by recorded digests. Class 1 blades rotate about the entity position (the affine double-size placement is not modelled), and the class 4 casing and impact come from the object library. The Python weapon writer is removed.

title: Music and sound effects
limitations: Zero Mission only: its sound bank and engine tables are exported privately; the music and the sound effects of the ported systems (Samus, weapons, hatches, blocks, enemies, drops) play through the ported engine, with the item jingles inserted in front of the music and the current track replayed after them, and the Chozo hint music; the audio device pulls the sound frame by frame at the hardware's 65.536 kHz rate (resampled by SDL), so game slowdowns cannot starve it; not yet compared with hardware. Liquids, ground effects, charge beams, bombs and bosses have no sounds yet. Aria of Sorrow audio is not started.

title: Zero Mission enemy sprites, effects, room placements and sprite tables
limitations: Only sprites with a ported AI are exported (Zoomers, Zeelas, Rippers, Skrees and their explosion parts, red Zeela eyes, Wavers, Sidehoppers, Dessgeegas including the Long Beam one, Violas, Sovas, Zebs, Geegas, Zebbos, Reos, Mellas, Holtzes, Multiviolas, Rinkas, Gerutas, Ripper IIs, Squeepts, Gamets, Skulteras, Dragons, the elevator pads, water drops, steam vents, Gerons, unknown item blocks, map stations, save platforms (with their row 2 flash), Space Pirates and their lasers, searchlights, security lasers and searchlight eyes), plus the enemy drops, the ported particle effects and sprite debris, and the message banner with the save prompt's cursor; hard-mode and event spritesets are not resolved; the baked frozen and stun variants take frozenPaletteRowOffset as 0. The native C11 metroid_sprites rebuild task writes all 20,088 sequences, 117,235 frames and 27,806 unique BMPs, the OAM bounds and sprites.tsv, byte-identical to the former Python writer; the ported sprites' tables are a generated copy of the pinned decompilation and recorded digests guard the index, bounds, tables and object names.

title: Zero Mission projectile sprites
